messages.content:
Generate Python code based on the following instruction. Output ONLY code. DO NOT include explanations or other textual content.
Instruction: Generate code that calculates the average elemental stress on a given volume using the pydpf-core library. The code should first create a model targeting a given result file and get all node IDs in the model to find the minimum amount of surrounding elements to get a minimum volume. Then, it should read the volume by element and find the minimum list of elements by node to get the volume check. After that, the code should create a workflow to compute equivalent stress averaged on elements, apply dot product seqv.volume, sum up those on the list of elements, and divide this sum by the total volume on these elements. Finally, the code should plot equivalent elemental stress and volume averaged elemental equivalent stress, and use the operator with the same algorithm that has been implemented.

message.content:
```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from ansys.dpf import core as dpf
from ansys.dpf.core import operators as ops

# Path to the result file
result_file = "path/to/your/result_file.rst"

# Load the model
model = dpf.Model(result_file)

# Get all node IDs
mesh = model.metadata.meshed_region
all_node_ids = mesh.nodes.scoping.ids

# Find the node with the minimum number of surrounding elements
min_elem_count = float('inf')
min_node_id = None
node_to_elems = {}
for node_id in all_node_ids:
    elems = mesh.elements_scoping_by_node(node_id)
    node_to_elems[node_id] = elems
    if len(elems) < min_elem_count:
        min_elem_count = len(elems)
        min_node_id = node_id

# Get the minimum list of elements by node
min_elem_list = node_to_elems[min_node_id]

# Read the volume by element
vol_op = ops.mesh.volume(mesh=mesh)
vol_field = vol_op.outputs.field()
elem_ids = vol_field.scoping.ids
elem_volumes = {eid: vol_field.get_entity_data_by_id(eid)[0] for eid in elem_ids}

# Get the total volume for the minimum element list
selected_elem_volumes = [elem_volumes[eid] for eid in min_elem_list]
total_volume = sum(selected_elem_volumes)

# Compute equivalent stress averaged on elements
seqv_op = ops.result.stress_eqv(model)
seqv_op.inputs.requested_location.connect("elemental")
seqv_field = seqv_op.outputs.fields_container()[0]

# Get equivalent stress for the selected elements
elem_seqv = {eid: seqv_field.get_entity_data_by_id(eid)[0] for eid in min_elem_list}

# Compute dot product seqv.volume, sum, and divide by total volume
weighted_sum = sum(elem_seqv[eid] * elem_volumes[eid] for eid in min_elem_list)
avg_elem_stress = weighted_sum / total_volume

# Plot equivalent elemental stress
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.bar([str(eid) for eid in min_elem_list], [elem_seqv[eid] for eid in min_elem_list])
plt.xlabel("Element ID")
plt.ylabel("Equivalent Elemental Stress")
plt.title("Equivalent Elemental Stress for Selected Elements")
plt.show()

# Plot volume averaged elemental equivalent stress
plt.figure(figsize=(5, 5))
plt.bar(["Volume Averaged Stress"], [avg_elem_stress])
plt.ylabel("Volume Averaged Equivalent Stress")
plt.title("Volume Averaged Elemental Equivalent Stress")
plt.show()

# Use the operator with the same algorithm
avg_stress_op = ops.math.weighted_average()
avg_stress_op.inputs.fields_container.connect(seqv_op.outputs.fields_container())
avg_stress_op.inputs.weights.connect(vol_op.outputs.field())
avg_stress_op.inputs.scoping.connect(dpf.Scoping(ids=min_elem_list, location="element"))
avg_stress = avg_stress_op.outputs.field().data[0]

print("Manual Computed Volume Averaged Stress:", avg_elem_stress)
print("Operator Computed Volume Averaged Stress:", avg_stress)
```
